correctness.rationale: The five preconditional laws and three additional F-algebra requirements are stated with full quantifiers. Order-reversing double-negation inflation gives the self-adjoint polarity, while semicomplementation gives looplessness, hence a unique simple graph for every induced negation. A two-atom antecedent admits exactly three singleton-output shapes by P2 and the idempotence instance of P5, and all remaining P5 instances reduce to two explicitly stated singleton-negation comparisons. These give independent row counts of 729,81,16,1 by graph type; Burnside fixed counts 1021,41,10 give 194 classes. The explicit graph constructor satisfies each defining law on any powerset. Two standalone computational derivations agree exactly, but do not substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: The eight-element Boolean algebra is the first Boolean carrier whose nontrivial intermediate two-atom antecedents force P5 compatibility constraints. The complete operation classification and 194 isomorphism classes are natural data for finite nonclassical conditional semantics, not a random parameter slice. Stratifying 1021 operations by all four graph types identifies exactly how a fixed weak negation leaves freedom in binary conditionals. The all-set graph realization links the finite census to a structural semantics valid at arbitrary cardinality and highlights a plausible path to larger finite-carrier classification.
